CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left wrist pain and bilateral hand numbness and tingling.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents with several months of left wrist pain and numbness and tingling in bilateral hands, predominantly affecting the left side. Onset was insidious with no identified precipitating event. Symptoms are worse at night, with patient waking up with numb hands requiring shaking to alleviate symptoms. Pain and numbness are present in all fingers but most prominent in the thumb and index finger, with occasional involvement of the fifth finger. Patient reports associated left hand weakness with difficulty grasping and dropping objects due to decreased sensation. Patient works in landscaping and yard work performing repetitive heavy labor.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for numbness and tingling in bilateral hands (predominantly left) and left hand weakness. Denies other systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Denies history of rheumatoid arthritis. No other significant past medical history reported.

MEDICATIONS
No current medications reported.

ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Occupation: Landscaping and yard work specializing in maintenance and flower beds involving repetitive heavy labor and digging. Alcohol use: 1-2 beers on weekends (Fridays and Saturdays). Denies tobacco and illicit drug use.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs
Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally
Musculoskeletal: Grip strength decreased on left compared to right. Sensation intact bilaterally in all fingers with subjective sensation changes noted on left thumb. Tinel's sign positive bilaterally at wrists with reproduction of tingling and zing in fingertips.

RESULTS
Electromyography (EMG) ordered to measure electrical impulses in fingers and assist in confirming diagnosis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, predominantly left-sided, likely secondary to occupational repetitive strain from landscaping work. Patient counseled on activity modification, delegating heavier work tasks to employees for approximately 2 weeks to minimize repetitive motions. Wrist splint prescribed for symptom management. Ibuprofen 600 mg orally every 6 hours prescribed. EMG study to be performed. Follow-up office visit in 2 weeks. Will reassess at follow-up for need for additional diagnostic testing or potential surgical intervention (carpal tunnel release) based on EMG results and response to conservative management.
